[[File:Chris Wondolowski.jpg|thumb|upright|[[Chris Wondolowski]] became the MLS all-time leading goalscorer on May 18, 2019.]]
This is a list of '''players who scored over 100 goals in [[Major League Soccer]]''', the top flight men's soccer league of the United States and Canada, dating back to its inaugural season in [[1996 Major League Soccer season|1996]]. This list does not include goals scored in the [[MLS Cup playoffs]]. Thirteen players have reached the milestone.

The first MLS player to reach 100 goals was [[Jason Kreis]] on August 13, 2005, with his goal in [[Real Salt Lake]]'s 4–2 loss to the Kansas City Wizards (now [[Sporting Kansas City]]).<ref>{{cite news |title=Soccer: Kreis is first MLS player with 100 goals |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/soccer-kreis-is-first-mls-player-with-100-goals/ |access-date=October 8, 2018 |work=Seattle Times |agency=Associated Press |date=August 14, 2005}}</ref> On August 22, 2007, [[Jaime Moreno (footballer, born 1974)|Jaime Moreno]] took the record from Kreis with his 109th goal, a penalty in a 3–1 win over his former team the [[New York Red Bulls]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Taylor |first1=Adam M. |title=D.C. United vs. New York Red Bulls - Throwback Thursday: Jaime Moreno sets *the* record |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/d-c-united-vs-york-171644942.html?guccounter=1 |access-date=October 8, 2018 |agency=SB Nation |publisher=Yahoo! |date=August 28, 2014}}</ref> Moreno retired in 2010 with 133 goals and held the record until August 27, 2011, when [[Jeff Cunningham]] scored his final MLS goal for [[Columbus Crew SC]] in their 6–2 defeat at [[Seattle Sounders FC]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCarthy |first1=Kyle |title=Monday MLS Breakdown: Jeff Cunningham claims MLS goalscoring record in his own way |url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/1110/major-league-soccer/2011/08/29/2641669/monday-mls-breakdown-jeff-cunningham-claims-mls-goalscoring |access-date=October 8, 2018 |publisher=Goal.com |date=August 29, 2011}}</ref> On May 25, 2014, [[Landon Donovan]] broke the record with his 135th goal in a 4–1 [[Los Angeles Galaxy]] win over the [[Philadelphia Union]];<ref>{{cite news |title=The Goal King! LA Galaxy's Landon Donovan sets new MLS goal record |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2014/05/26/goal-king-la-galaxys-landon-donovan-sets-new-mls-goal-record |access-date=October 8, 2018 |publisher=Major League Soccer |date=May 25, 2014}}</ref> he retired in 2016 with 145 goals. The record was subsequently broken on May 18, 2019, as [[Chris Wondolowski]] scored his 146th goal in a 4–1 win for the [[San Jose Earthquakes]] over the [[Chicago Fire Soccer Club|Chicago Fire]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chris Wondolowski breaks MLS all-time scoring record |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/05/18/chris-wondolowski-scores-goal-no-146-breaks-mls-all-time-goals-record |access-date=May 19, 2019 |publisher=Major League Soccer |date=May 19, 2019 |archive-date=June 18, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190618085029/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/05/18/chris-wondolowski-scores-goal-no-146-breaks-mls-all-time-goals-record |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Of the thirteen players, eight are Americans and one, [[Dwayne De Rosario]], is Canadian. The highest-scoring foreigner is [[Kei Kamara]] of Sierra Leone, with 147 goals. Kamara moved to the U.S. as a refugee at 16 and attended high school and college in the U.S. before turning pro. [[Jaime Moreno (footballer, born 1974)|Jaime Moreno]] of Bolivia and [[Bradley Wright-Phillips]] of England are the highest scoring players from South America and Europe respectively.
